Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

fastkcv 0.1.0

First release.

  • kcv(): exact leave-one-out and k-fold cross-validation for global simple, ordinary and universal kriging from one factorization of the covariance matrix. Same inputs (formula, locations, data, model, nfold, beta) and output as gstat::krige.cv(), for data.frame, sf and sp data; variogram models Nug, Exp, Sph, Gau, Mat, Ste, Cir, Pen, Bes, Wav, Hol, nested sums and 2D geometric anisotropy.
  • kcv_prepare() and kcv_run(): factorize once, cross-validate any number of fold schemes.
  • Buffered leave-one-out (buffer), optionally for a subset of targets.
  • Several responses from one factorization: a matrix left-hand side (cbind(z1, z2) ~ 1, or a matrix column) in kcv() and kcv_prepare(), and new responses for a prepared object with kcv_run(prepared, y = ), for every fold scheme and buffered leave-one-out. The output stacks one block per response with a response column; kcv_metrics() summarizes each response. Simple kriging takes one beta for all responses or a p x T matrix (also in kcv_run(beta = ) and kcv_engine_run(beta = )).
  • kcv_engine(), kcv_engine_prepare() and kcv_engine_run(): the same computation from a precomputed covariance matrix, also for a matrix-valued response.
  • Fold builders fold_random() (the same draw as krige.cv(nfold = k)), fold_blocks() and fold_kmeans().
  • kcv_metrics(): RMSE, MAE, bias, z-score mean and variance, and prediction-interval coverage, overall or per fold.
  • Memory requirements are checked up front against getOption("fastkcv.max_gb").
  • Ordinary and universal kriging estimate the trend in an orthonormal basis of the trend matrix, so trends in large raw coordinates (such as a quadratic trend in UTM meters) stay accurate.
